This is an existing Claude project, so I would use the Claude initialization route and preserve the current CLAUDE.md and settings permission policies. I have only inspected the supplied old initialization skill; no real project has been mutated.

First inspect CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, existing hooks, init.sh, architecture docs, manifests and CI configuration. Establish the actual language, framework, package manager, project type, test framework and team size from local evidence. Network access is unavailable, so use only locally installed templates and skills; report missing resources instead of pretending they were fetched or installing a substitute from the network. Test commands are unknown: discover them from scripts, CI and existing documentation, then verify their behavior locally where dependencies are available. Do not invent a passing type-check command or create an exit-0 quality gate.

The old skill's Existing Project Mode explicitly asks the user to choose incremental addition, optimize/consolidate, or backed-up full rebuild. My recommendation is incremental addition because existing permission policies and instructions must survive. For an actual execution, present the inspected contents and a concrete additive patch, then request that choice before any replacement. The source is prior-skills/init/SKILL.md, which states: "Do not overwrite existing files — only replace after the user explicitly confirms." Its workflow also requires a CLAUDE.md backup before execution. The present request is only to describe the approach, so no approval is needed to perform this evaluation.

After an authorized choice, back up CLAUDE.md without overwriting a pre-existing backup, add only missing sections, and merge settings structurally while preserving existing allow/deny permissions and hook registrations. Prepare SessionStart, Stop type-check, sensitive-file protection and formatter hooks from locally available language-appropriate templates, along with the three planning/TDD/verification skills, init.sh, an architecture map, ADR index, progress skeleton and archive directory. Do not manufacture historical ADR decisions. Whether root features.json is required depends on team size; the old skill treats it as human-maintained/read-only and contains a conflicting later diagram showing docs/features.json, so use the explicit root-location instruction and flag that inconsistency rather than creating two authoritative copies.

Check JSON and shell syntax, inspect the settings diff for preserved permission policies, ensure hook scripts are executable, validate registration and actual success/failure behavior, confirm architecture dependency rules and ADR links, and run bash init.sh for the status summary. Run discovered tests and type checks only when their commands and dependencies are known. Unknown test commands or unavailable local templates block verified initialization; report exactly what remains unchecked. The old skill asks for CLAUDE.md at most 60 lines, but incremental adoption may exceed that target; disclose that result and propose a separate approved consolidation rather than deleting existing rules to force the number.

No commit, issue sync, push, deploy, global settings changes or network operation is authorized. Initialization must not be described as complete merely because files or hook entries exist. A later execution report would list the actual generated files, checks run, unresolved gaps and a two-week observation period before further audit/evolution.
